name: Importance-Weighted Stochastic Sampling for Gaussian Simplification
definition: A simplification strategy that replaces deterministic pruning of Gaussians with stochastic sampling to preserve local geometry. Deterministic pruning disrupts geometry because neighboring Gaussians have similar importance and are removed/preserved simultaneously, leading to suboptimal results measured by chamfer distance.
summary: Importance-Weighted Stochastic Sampling for Gaussian Simplification reduces Gaussian counts by randomly selecting Gaussians based on importance scores, preserving local geometry better than deterministic pruning.
